questions.question: A man invested (1)/(3) of his income at 7% simple interest, (1)/(4) of his income at 8% simple interest, and the remainder of his income at 10% simple interest. If the total interest at the end of one year was ₹561, what was his initial income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume **Total Income** = 1200 units (LCM of 3 and 4 multiplied by 100 for easy calculation).

**Part 1:** 1/3 of 1200 = 400 units @ 7% interest = 28 units.

**Part 2:** 1/4 of 1200 = 300 units @ 8% interest = 24 units.

**Part 3:** Remaining (1200 − 700) = 500 units @ 10% interest = 50 units.

Total Interest = 28 + 24 + 50 = 102 units → ₹561.

1 unit = 561 ÷ 102 = 5.5. Therefore, 1200 units = 1200 × 5.5 = ₹6,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total interest = ₹561, Time = 1 year, **Rates** = 7%, 8%, 10%.

**Formula Used:** Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf3637ed6b137e382673f72c4d23eb9f36db973410c4703562cf15564133c1ac.png] 

Let the total income be x.

⇒ Interest from Part 1 = (x ÷ 3) × (7 ÷ 100) = 7x ÷ 300

⇒ Interest from Part 2 = (x ÷ 4) × (8 ÷ 100) = 8x ÷ 400 = 2x ÷ 100

⇒ Remainder part = x − (x ÷ 3 + x ÷ 4) = x − (7x ÷ 12) = 5x ÷ 12

⇒ Interest from Part 3 = (5x ÷ 12) × (10 ÷ 100) = 50x ÷ 1200 = 5x ÷ 120

⇒ Total Interest = (7x ÷ 300) + (2x ÷ 100) + (5x ÷ 120) = 561

⇒ (28x + 24x + 50x) ÷ 1200 = 561

⇒ 102x ÷ 1200 = 561

⇒ x = (561 × 1200) ÷ 102

⇒ x = 11 × 600 = 6600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest on Different Parts

When a sum is divided into parts P₁, P₂, ..., Pₙ at rates R₁, R₂, ..., Rₙ, the total interest is the sum of interest from each part: Total I = Σ(Pᵢ × Rᵢ × Tᵢ) ÷ 100.

Effective Rate of Interest

The combined or average rate for multiple investments can be calculated as Rₑff = (Total Interest × 100) ÷ (Total Principal × Time).

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount A after time T is given by A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

questions.question: In what duration will a sum of money double itself at 10% per annum rate of simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

When a sum of money **doubles** itself, the **Simple Interest** earned is exactly 100% of the **Principal**.

Shortcut formula for doubling: **Time (T) = 100 ÷ Rate (R)**

Given **Rate = 10%** per annum.

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 10 = 10 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Rate (R)** = 10% per annum

Let the **Principal (P)** = ₹100

Since the sum **doubles** itself, the **Amount (A)** = 2 × 100 = ₹200

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100**

**Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61a6382b239d1389a9e4385ec78b939418be96f3b7362a0ccb27a6ff3df49396.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 200 − 100 = ₹100

Now, substituting values in the **Simple Interest** formula:

⇒ 100 = (100 × 10 × T) ÷ 100

⇒ 100 = 10 × T

⇒ T = 100 ÷ 10

⇒ T = 10 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

n-times the Sum (Simple Interest)

If a sum of money becomes **n** times itself at **R%** rate of interest, the time **T** is given by: T = (n − 1) × 100 ÷ R.

Relationship between Rate and Time

For a fixed amount of **Simple Interest**, the **Rate** of interest and **Time** are inversely proportional (R ∝ 1/T).

Rule of 72 (Compound Interest)

In **Compound Interest**, the time required to double a sum is approximately T ≈ 72 ÷ R (where R is the annual interest rate).

questions.question: A sum of money lent on simple interest becomes (7)/(5) of itself in 4 years. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **Principal (P)** be 5 units (denominator of the fraction).

The **Amount (A)** becomes 7 units (numerator of the fraction).

**Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal = 7 − 5 = 2 units.

**Rate (R)** = (Interest ÷ Principal) × (100 ÷ Time).

Rate = (2 ÷ 5) × (100 ÷ 4) = 0.4 × 25 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount (A) = 7/5 of Principal (P)

Time period (T) = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0163fedb9544edf29d1eff4c42083932868027ca2e2b7547187d2410a17224f4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = (7/5)P − P = (2/5)P

⇒ SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

⇒ (2/5)P = (P × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 2/5 = 4R ÷ 100

⇒ 2/5 = R ÷ 25

⇒ R = (2 × 25) ÷ 5

⇒ R = 10%

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between Amount and Rate

The amount in simple interest can be directly calculated using the formula A = P(1 + RT/100), where R is the **annual rate** and T is the **time in years**.

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective rate for the entire duration is (R × T)%. In this case, 10% × 4 = 40%, which matches the interest being 2/5 (or 40%) of the principal.

Simple Interest vs Compound Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant every year as it is always calculated on the original **Principal**, unlike Compound Interest where interest is earned on interest.</p

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum will ₹1,300 give ₹520 as simple interest in 5 years?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Interest for 1 year = **Total Interest** ÷ **Time** = 520 ÷ 5 = ₹104.

**Rate %** = (Interest for 1 year ÷ **Principal**) × 100

**Rate %** = (104 ÷ 1300) × 100 = 8%.

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,300

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹520

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d4ca9f1e2134f4aac8643cb47eb0a700046ce3bac47b636f793b4a6e40ce4915.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 520 = (1300 × R × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ 520 = 13 × R × 5

⇒ 520 = 65 × R

⇒ R = 520 ÷ 65

⇒ R = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Total Amount (A)

The total amount returned after the time period is the sum of Principal and Interest: A = P + SI.

Finding Time (T)

If the Rate and Principal are known, Time can be calculated as: T = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R).

Constant Interest Property

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains the same for every year as it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Rate-Time Product

The total interest percentage relative to the principal is always the product of Rate and Time (R × T) percent.

questions.question: What sum will earn a simple interest of ₹480 in 3 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total **Percentage Interest** for 3 years = Rate × Time = 16% × 3 = 48%

Given that 48% of the **Principal** = ₹480

1% of the **Principal** = 480 ÷ 48 = 10

100% (**Total Sum**) = 10 × 100 = ₹1,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹480

**Time** (T) = 3 years

**Rate of Interest** (R) = 16% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/991ea5d2d616b1a878b568a14925cad71822825be6d9757a1539eef1ead0c69a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 480 = (P × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 480 = (P × 48) ÷ 100

⇒ P × 48 = 480 × 100

⇒ P = (480 × 100) ÷ 48

⇒ P = 10 × 100

⇒ P = 1,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. The formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is **Principal**, R is **Rate**, and T is **Time**.

Total Amount Formula

The total amount (A) after T years is the sum of the principal and the interest earned: A = P + SI = P × (1 + RT/100).

Rate and Time Relation

If the rate of interest is given per month, the time must also be in months, or both must be converted to an **annual basis** for calculation consistency.

questions.question: Find the simple interest on ₹3,000 as a sum borrowed at 4% per year rate of interest for 5 years.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total interest percentage = **Rate** × **Time**

Net Interest % = 4% × 5 = 20%

Simple Interest = 20% of ₹3,000 = (20 ÷ 100) × 3,000

Simple Interest = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹3,000

**Rate (R)** = 4% per year

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d300e6686611ddf517063a06ef58be5c251fac190b18469c8d0c6f7f18c20c3b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = (3000 × 4 × 5) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (3000 × 20) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 30 × 20

⇒ SI = ₹600

Therefore, the calculated value matches **Option (3)**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

Simple interest is calculated only on the initial principal amount. Formula: SI = P × R × T ÷ 100.

Total Amount

The total sum paid at the end of the duration is Principal + Interest. Amount (A) = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Interest Rate Units

The Rate (R) and Time (T) must be in the same time units (e.g., both per year or both per month) before calculation.

questions.question: How long will it take for ₹1,500 to become ₹2,040 at a rate of 8% per annum simple interest?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Interest** per year = 8% of ₹1,500 = ₹120.

Total **Simple Interest** needed = ₹2,040 − ₹1,500 = ₹540.

**Time** = Total Interest ÷ Interest per year.

⇒ **Time** = 540 ÷ 120 = 4.5 years.

4.5 years is equal to 4 1/2 years, which matches **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 1/2 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,500

**Amount (A)** = ₹2,040

**Rate (R)** = 8% per annum

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/585e652359703320ca3bcb7d29303f0b7f60816529733a4e5c4d445be036aeb2.png] 

**Formula Used:**

**Simple Interest (SI)** = Amount − Principal

**Time (T)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R)

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Simple Interest (SI)** = 2040 − 1500 = 540

⇒ **T** = (540 × 100) ÷ (1500 × 8)

⇒ **T** = 54000 ÷ 12000

⇒ **T** = 54 ÷ 12

⇒ **T** = 4.5 years

⇒ **T** = 4 1/2 years

Thus, the time required is 4 1/2 years, which is given in **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4 1/2 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

The basic formula is SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100, where P is **Principal**, R is **Rate** per annum, and T is **Time** in years.

Total Amount

The total **Amount (A)** accumulated after a period is the sum of the Principal and the Interest: A = P + SI.

Time Conversion

Always ensure **Time (T)** is in years if the Rate is per annum. If time is in months, divide by 12; if in days, divide by 365.

Difference between SI and CI

In **Simple Interest**, interest is calculated only on the initial principal, whereas in **Compound Interest**, interest is calculated on the principal plus accumulated interest.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Principal = 100%. Simple Interest for 3 years at 20% = 20% × 3 = 60%.

Amount after 3 years = 100% + 60% = 160% ⇒ 160% = ₹2400.

Simple Interest for 2 years at same rate = 20% × 2 = 40%.

Since 160% = ₹2400, then 40% = (2400 ÷ 160) × 40 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Amount after 3 years (A) = ₹2400

Time (T₁) = 3 years

Time (T₂) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P + (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 100% (P)
 
 
 60% (3yr SI)
 
 

 Amount = 160% = ₹2400
 
 
 40% (2yr SI)
 
 

 2400 ÷ 4 = ₹600

⇒ Let the principal be P.

⇒ Amount after 3 years = P + (P × 20 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 2400 = P + 0.6P

⇒ 1.6P = 2400

⇒ Simple Interest for 2 years = (P × R × T₂) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (1500 × 20 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = ₹600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest (SI)

It is calculated only on the initial principal sum for the entire duration. Formula: SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100.

Compound Interest (CI)

Interest is calculated on the initial principal and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods. Formula: A = P(1 + R/100)T.

Percentage Approach for SI

Effective SI rate for T years at R% per annum is strictly (R × T)%. Total Amount becomes (100 + RT)% of the Principal.

questions.question: A sum, when invested at 20% simple interest per annum, amounts to ₹2880 after 4 years. What is the simple interest (in ₹) on the same sum at the same rate in 2 year?

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) / 100

Amount (A) = P + SI

Let the Principal amount be P.

Amount (A) = P + SI

SI for 4 years = (P × 20 × 4) / 100

SI for 4 years = (80P) / 100 = 0.8P

⇒ P + 0.8P = 2880

⇒ 1.8P = 2880

⇒ P = 2880 / 1.8 = 1600

Now, we need to find the simple interest for 2 years at the same rate.

SI for 2 years = (1600 × 20 × 2) / 100 = (64000) / 100 = 640

**The simple interest on the same sum at the same rate in 2 years is ₹640.**
